keep_playing_why: In A the single verb (pull or push the tide) is also the obstacle, so every place reframed it: low for the causeway, high for the well, a narrow shifting band through the Needles, and a lure-strand-slam rhythm against the Undertow. I changed how I played within minutes. B never made me decide anything I had not seen in a hundred tower defenses, and its economy flooded me.
better_made_why: A has a hand-made world, NPC dialogue that teaches by feedback, per-zone music and a proper ending card, though it has black transition frames, a drown-respawn soft-lock and an invisible pots side quest. B is cleaner and more bug-free, with excellent hit sounds, readable UI and stage music, but its menus occasionally swallowed taps and the economy and difficulty curve are untuned.
furthest_A: Completed the full main line at ~530 s: harbour, well shard, Tam's boat, Shellflats wreck lens, Needles by boat, stepping stones to the Stack, beat the Undertow in 3 phases, lit the lamp, got the end card (9 min, 82 m of sea moved, 11 knocks, 0 of 5 lost things found). Never found Marta's pots.
furthest_B: Stage 1 The Cutting Board cleared with 3 stars; stage 2 The Stovetop lost to the Jar then beaten on retry (1 star); stage 3 The Sink at wave 3 of 10 at the 540 s mark.
